kind: interactive coding agent and separately exported agent runtimes

runtime.execution: Ordinary CLI uses AgentSession over Agent/agent-loop in Node/Bun; codemode creates a fresh QuickJS worker sandbox per action. Separate exported durable/Pico3 harnesses are experimental and not transferred to baseline CLI claims.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns local conversation tree, extension contexts and launched shell/stdio children; consumes provider runtimes, HTTP MCP services and injectable remote filesystem/process backends. Chord/durable runtime APIs exist separately.

summary: A small default coding tool set with unusually broad executable extension hooks, actual source-code tool composition, branch-local JSON state and provenance-preserving context projections; experimental durable runtime surfaces require distinct study.

inspection.scope: CLI SDK/session/loop/provider/tool boundaries, built-in code mode and nested calls, compaction/context edits/history access, reload/cancellation, MCP lifecycle and local test oracles read; experimental harness API/lifecycle and status documentation read separately.
inspection.limits: No runtime/test execution. Durable operation state machine, Chord scheduler, full transport internals and all optional extensions not exhaustively traced. Do not apply experimental-harness documented recovery or plugin test behavior to the default CLI.

filesystem.detail: Default read/write/edit and optional search tools use injectable operation backends; local mutations serialize until in-flight IO settles.

processes.detail: bash streams detached shell execution, has optional deadline and explicit abort/tree-kill requests, exit code/full-output metadata. Persistent public PTY/process handles were not established.

code_actions.detail: Built-in, initially inactive codemode exposes model-authored JavaScript that composes actual tools through nested validation/hooks with structured results and explicit output filtering.

persistent_kernel.detail: Each codemode action creates/closes a fresh QuickJS sandbox. Successful JSON store writes persist on the branch, but functions/live interpreter state do not persist through that mechanism.

standing_database.detail: Branch-local store/load reconstructs structured JSON values from session custom entries and extensions have history APIs. It supplies key-value state, not a separately owned standing SQL/query service.

workflow_programming.detail: Codemode provides actual loops/chains/parallel calls; extension tools/commands and tool/turn/context hooks compose normal operation. No default general graph scheduler is inferred.

multi_model.detail: Current model refreshes at next assistant request; extension model/provider mutation and script catalog/classifier calls are exposed. Classifier fan-out is distinct from independently working chat peers.

live_collaboration.detail: Inspected baseline prompt/queue/extension/code-mode paths address one session and nested tool calls. No arbitrary addressed messages between independently running chat participants were established; experimental multiple conversations alone are insufficient.

concurrent_work.detail: Agent tool batches and codemode Promise composition run independent calls concurrently while sequential tools serialize; nested calls have meaningful parent IDs. This does not establish a standing multi-agent room.

steering_interrupt.detail: Steering waits for current assistant tools and follow-up waits for run completion. abort cancels agent/summary/retry work and waits idle; shell cancellation invokes termination.

turn_redefinition.detail: Actual finishTurn/prepareNextTurn/prepareRequest decisions can change continuation, model, tools and context; CLI wires extension turn-end continuation and post-run before-settle continuation. Scope is these boundaries, not arbitrary replacement of active stack frames.

compaction.detail: Manual/auto compaction is managed and cancellable, with extension replacement, retained entry ID and persisted metadata; active projection selects summary/tail from immutable branch entries.

context_repair.detail: Append-only branch-local context edits can omit/restore content while retaining original entry IDs/content. Extensions can retrieve originals/tree and project lineage, but a dedicated model repair workflow is composed rather than a default native tool.

original_audit.detail: Append-only message/context-edit lineage and provider hooks are useful. Nested records deliberately omit/drop/clip data under budgets, script nested results do not all reach model transcript, and exact forced prompt rendering is not recorded; full original audit is not established.

audit_query.detail: Extensions receive sessionManager and can fetch branch/all-entry/tree/source projection; models may compose access through extension tools. Inspected scope is session history, not an established complete provider/program audit query corpus.

hot_change.detail: Reload rebuilds resource/provider/extension runtime with stale-context invalidation while preserving session. CLI refuses reload during streaming or compaction; tool/model refresh is next-request. Programmatic reload does not itself show the same guard or Arconaut's affected-workflow deferred activation.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Resource reload preserves conversation and invalidates old extension handles, but it does not replace the harness executable. Separate experimental suspend/close APIs do not establish a CLI outpost compile-and-reinhabit protocol or survival of live OS effects.

remote_services.detail: MCP consumes HTTP services or launches configured stdio servers; lazy getClient/explicit reconnect and resource/tool APIs are wired. Filesystem/bash operations can be supplied by remote backends; shared service governance is not inferred.

self_improvement.detail: Model code actions and reloadable extensions allow substantial alteration, but the inspected paths do not establish a dedicated model-governed candidate evaluation/promotion/autoresearch loop.

complaints.detail: Inspected native tools, extensions and session lifecycle do not establish a default model complaint operation that captures state and tracks follow-up. Custom extension composition remains possible.

authority.detail: Local tools directly operate with launcher authority; before-tool hooks can block/terminate and nested calls use the same pipeline. README documents no built-in restrictive permission system; extensions can add policy.

evaluation.detail: Read tests attack projection/original separation, nested ID/usage/concurrency and explicit record truncation, plus separate experimental facet cutover. Fake tools/in-memory sessions/stub lane limit integration claims; tests not run.

time_order.detail: Append-only entries carry parent IDs/wall timestamps; nested durations use performance.now, shell seconds deadlines and script hard deadlines. Restart/paused-time guarantees for default CLI were not established.

evidence.claim: prompt intercepts extension commands/input and queues steer/followUp during a run.
CLI/SDK creates ordinary Agent and AgentSession with provider stream, context and provider event hooks.
Loop applies prepareNextTurn/prepareRequest, steering, tool-call settlement and finishTurn continuation decisions; truncated tool-call arguments are failed.
Context is transformed/converted and current model stream called with key and AbortSignal.
Tool batches choose sequential or parallel execution; parallel outcomes materialize in assistant source order.
Tool arguments are validated, beforeToolCall can block/terminate, and abort is checked before effects.
Extension turn-end continuation and next-request context/tool/model refresh are wired to Agent callbacks.
Nested/direct tool call and result interception uses the current extension runner and parent call identity.
Eight native tool names are exported; default coding tools are read/bash/edit/write.
bash accepts command and optional seconds timeout; structured results include capped combined output, full path, exit code and wall time.
Local shell spawns detached where available, streams stdout/stderr and invokes process-tree kill on abort/deadline.
read has path/offset/limit and injectable filesystem operations backed by local reads.
write resolves path, serializes file mutation and retains the queue until in-flight IO settles even after abort.
edit validates path/edits and applies unique disjoint replacements to original content inside the mutation queue.
grep takes pattern, path, glob, ignoreCase, literal, context and limit.
find takes pattern/path/limit; registered execution has abort/child stop handling.
ls resolves a directory, reads entries and sorts/formats a bounded result.
Built-in codemode registers inactive; explicit activation or MCP integration exposes it.
A fresh bounded QuickJS sandbox routes nested calls through ctx.executeTool, closes after execution, persists successful store writes and returns clipped script output/errors.
codemode takes source code and documents tools/discovery/output/JSON store helpers, no direct Node/FS/network/timers and script deadline options.
JSON store is reconstructed from custom entries on the selected branch.
Script model catalog and classifier calls are wired, with four-call concurrency limiting and attributed usage.
Manual compaction can be canceled/replaced by extension, persists summary/firstKeptEntryId and refreshes active projection.
Automatic compaction uses the same replaceable summary path, checks abort and emits managed events.
Active context selects compaction/retained entries and overlays latest context edits while exposing sourceEntry provenance.
appendContextEdit validates branch-local targets and replacement shape without rewriting original message content.
Branch/tree/all-entry retrieval is separate from compaction-aware context projection; append-only entry history remains accessible.
Extensions receive the sessionManager with stale-runner checks.
Steering is queued until after current assistant tools; follow-up waits until tool/steering work finishes.
abort cancels retry, compaction, branch summary and agent execution then waits for idle.
Reload shuts down/invalidate old extension contexts, reloads resources/providers/settings and builds a new extension runtime while keeping session state.
Interactive /reload refuses streaming/compaction, then rebuilds chat and keybindings around session reload.
Nested-call records omit arguments beyond byte budgets, drop calls past 256, clip errors and mark incompleteness; durations use performance.now.
Forced provider head prompt is projected without recording that exact rendering in the transcript.
Extension contract declares tool/command registration, messages, appendEntry, exec, active tools, model choice and immediate post-bind provider registration.
Configured MCP URL selects HTTP transport; command selects a stdio transport with cwd/env.
MCP getClient lazily reconnects and tool/resource calls consume service APIs.
Explicit reconnect drops old client and obtains a new one.
Pico3 is explicitly an experimental separate subpath, not the ordinary package-root CLI Agent loop.
Experimental harness exposes task kinds, conversations, commit/fork/collapse/reset/abort/watches and input handles.
Experimental harness exposes task marking/waiting and close via suspend; these do not establish CLI executable replacement.
Tests assert projection omission/restoration and original content retention with in-memory sessions.
Tests assert sequential/parallel concurrency and explicit argument/call/error recording caps using fake tools.
Experimental plugin test asserts new facet activation/old disposal using a stub lane, not default CLI continuity.
Official repository README states no built-in filesystem/process/network/credential permission system and inheritance of launcher authority.

tests.focus: Original/projection separation and branch-local content repair.
tests.oracle: In-memory assertions preserve original message while latest edit omits/restores projected content; no provider summary-faithfulness oracle.

tests.focus: Nested identity, usage, concurrency and explicit audit clipping.
tests.oracle: Fake tools assert sequential=1 versus parallel=3 and recorder caps/incompleteness; live services and durable crashes not tested in read cases.
Stub lane/loader records generations; proves that cutover contract locally, not baseline CLI executable continuity.

strengths: Executable code actions compose tools through the ordinary pipeline instead of bypassing hooks.
Original entry and current context projection are explicit separate concepts with append-only repair lineage.
Next-turn/settled boundaries expose continuation decisions and model/tool refresh.
Reload marks prior extension contexts stale, making invalid authority reuse explicit.
limits: Fresh code-mode sandbox persists JSON values only; it is not a live persistent kernel.
Normalized bounded nested-call records are not exhaustive original audit.
Default CLI and exported experimental durable/Pico3 runtimes must be kept distinct.
Interactive reload guards response/compaction but does not establish executable refit or model-governed experiment promotion.
arconaut_questions: Can Arconaut retain Pi's executable nested-tool ergonomics with an external shared kernel rather than owning interpreter lifetime?
Which context edit/compaction lineage should be model-addressable as normal agency, and how do we retain every original beside the projection?
Should explicit stale-context generations also fence extension/service authority across a quiescent refit?
What scope of pending workflows must delay a configuration change beyond a next-provider-request boundary?
